neighbours.label: a required or valued property in text about protection and security: what a protective mechanism must have or be capable of (the counterpart of the + pole's 'safe/secure' words)
fire: The strength of the cipher depends on the length of the key and on its randomness.
Password managers must be able to resist brute force and keep credentials private.
Firewall rules control who has access, and audit logs record each attempt.
The helmet must be rated to withstand a hard impact at high speed.
An effective identity check must confirm that every buyer is over eighteen.
The vault door is fire resistant, so documents inside will not be damaged.
Attackers value stolen logins because such data is a useful black-market commodity.
Antivirus tools need powerful scanners and frequent updates to stop new threats.
quiet: The flavor of the soup depends on the length of the simmer and on its seasoning.
Bread makers must be able to knead dough and keep loaves warm.
Library rules say who has borrowed, and ledgers record each loan.
The painting must be hung to catch a soft light in the afternoon.
A friendly host should greet every guest who is at the door.
The picnic table is made of pine, so children can sit around it.
Collectors value old stamps because such paper is a lovely keepsake.
Gardeners need sturdy boots and frequent breaks to enjoy long days.

notes: Top examples are scattered tokens (access, size, effective, capable) in security, PKI and safety-equipment text. Low confidence: the shared pattern may be topic only.
